newsitem.title: UGANDA: Uganda says 230 invaders killed in fighting.
newsitem.headline: Uganda says 230 invaders killed in fighting.

text.p: Ugandan President Yoweri Museveni said on Tuesday 230 invaders were killed and 30 taken prisoner in fighting in the southwest last week.
"According to my figures, so far we have counted 230 bodies of these poor boys, 112 guns captured from them and 30 (taken) prisoners of war," Museveni told a news conference in Kampala.
Museveni, whose cabinet had blamed the fighting in the region that borders Zaire on Zairean troops and Zaire-based Ugandan dissidents, linked the fighting to Sudan.

He said he had talked to Zairean President Mobutu Sese Seko and exonerated him from any involvement in the fighting in which at least 10 Ugandan soldiers were also killed and an estimated 70,000 to 75,000 people were forced to flee their homes.

"I have contacted Marshall Mobutu. Arabs are the ones behind this attack. It is Sudan; Sudan is acting through Zaire," Museveni said, laying blame at the feet of Sudanese Islamic leader Hassan al-Tourabi.
He suggested al-Tourabi supported Ugandan dissidents belonging to the Moslem fundamentalist Tabliq group, whom he largely blamed for orchestrating the fighting last week.
Museveni declared the fighting over and said peace was restored.

Museveni said other rebel groups -- such as the Lord's Resistance Army that wants to rule Uganda along the tenets of the Biblical Ten Commandments, and the West Nile Bank Front also received the support of Sudan and al-Tourabi.
"These groups have been coordinated by Sudan since May," Museveni told reporters.

He said his meeting with Sudanese President Omar Hassan al-Bashir in Rome, on the sidelines of the World Food Summit, meant nothing because "for me I don't put much hope in Bashir or Tourabi. They are not serious."
Last Wednesday, Uganda's Minister of State for Foreign Affairs Martin Aliker said the Ugandan army repulsed the attack and killed three invaders.
"Those who are foolish enough to engage in treason will perish," Museveni told reporters. "Those who try to capture power through unconstitutional means will be killed."

On Sunday, acting Ugandan Chief of Staff Brigadier Jerome Mugume said the invaders, calling themselves the Allied Democratic Force, were "thugs and dissidents" from a group formerly known as the National Army for the Liberation of Uganda (NALU) which was defeated more than a year ago.
He added that they were backed by a number of Zairean troops and had been trained in Zaire and Sudan to destabilize Uganda.
Zaire denied its troops were involved.
